text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Capital braces for violence.
- Israeli president, U.S. back Prime Minister Netanyahu's proposal for accelerated final status peace talks.
- Israel's Technion technical college to make second attempt to launch student-built satellite in summer.
- Widow of assassinated prime minister Rabin raps Israel's right wing in book due out in April excerpted in Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper.
- Finance Minister Meridor: slash tariffs on Jordanian imports.
HAARETZ
- Labour party leader Peres and challenger Barak clash over possibility of Labour joining national unity government.
- Special deployment out of fears of violence after Friday Moslem prayers.
- Air Force officer says he misspoke in testimony on recent helicopter accident that killed 73 Israeli soldiers.
- All plans to establish train lines other than suburban train frozen out of lack of budget.
- Shlomo Eliahu acquires 36 percent of Ayalon Insurance company for $11 million.
KOL HA-IR
- U.S. administration to Netanyahu: cancel house demolition orders against Palestinians in East Jerusalem as one among series of gestures to them compensating for new settlement.
MAARIV
- Defence minister warns of violence.
- Revelation: Netanyahu's plan for final status -- A Palestinian state in half of the West Bank, Jerusalem under Israeli sovereignty.
- State attorney under guard ahead of indictments in government corruption affair
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Netanyahu to Clinton: the peace process will collapse unless we immediately reach a final status agreement
- Police inclined to indict Justice Minister Tsachi Hanegbi and Shas party leader Arieh Deri in attorney-general appointment affair.
GLOBES
- Decision on interest rate on Sunday. Finance Minister Meridor: raising the interest after February CPI - a bad joke.
- Strauss will be forced to sell 5 pct of Reshet stock if he buys Federman's shares in Elite.
- Yaacov Bardugo, Galia Albin, submitted candidacy for directorship of Payis lottery
- Investigators in Bar-On affair examine possibility of questioning state attorney Arbel over Hanegbi statement to court
